note: Gemini ile sentezlenmiş, kural tabanlı biçimbilim denetiminden ve kör jüri incelemesinden geçmiş EĞİTİM/GELİŞTİRME kümesi. Tutulan test kümesi morph_eval_set_v1.3.1'dir ve bu dosyaya dahil değildir.

conventions.perspective: Documents are agent-memory records. First-person records refer to the user; third-person records refer to the named individual. Query person always matches the person of the target record.
conventions.query_rule: The query is a natural everyday recollection that ASSERTS the target state. Yes/no questions are forbidden (a passage answering either polarity would count as relevant, so polarity would not be discriminated). Meta-search phrasing such as 'kaydi ariyorum' / 'bul' is not used. Nominalised template queries were removed in v1.0.
conventions.positive_rule: The positive is an independent paraphrase of the target record. It must KEEP the query's content words (entities, objects, places) and re-realise only the morphological construction. Substituting a content noun with a synonym is forbidden: it injects a vocabulary-mismatch failure into a measurement that is meant to isolate suffix sensitivity. The positive must also carry the full target meaning - the critical content word may not be weakened to a looser near-synonym.

hard_negative_subtypes.morph_counterfactual: minimal suffix contrast with the positive; the main measurement target
hard_negative_subtypes.state_variant: different state, person, tense or participant
hard_negative_subtypes.same_feature_wrong_content: same suffix pattern, wrong content; blocks lexical shortcuts
hard_negative_subtypes.partial_trap: partially overlapping event with the opposite outcome

conventions.single_gold_rule: No candidate other than the positive may be a valid answer under any reading of the query.

tiers.hard: syntactically demanding structures (reciprocal, conditional, counterfactual, habitual)
tiers.minimal: positive and morph_counterfactual differ by exactly one word / one suffix

layers.chain: composition of two or more suffixes

slices.extended_hard: Harder variants added in v1.2, one per tier so far (more planned). standard: the critical suffix sits in a subordinate clause inside a longer passage padded with irrelevant filler (tests whether the signal survives mean pooling). hard: three or four suffixes whose scope order determines the meaning. minimal: positive and morph_counterfactual differ by exactly one morphological feature, often a single letter (gelmedi / gelemedi).
